documents.t: The WiFi LoRa 32 is a well-known IoT development board created by Heltec Automation. Since its release in 2017, it has been popular among developers and makers. The new V3 version keeps the same pin layout as the V2 and continues to support Wi-Fi, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), LoRa, and an OLED display. This board is ideal for applications in smart cities, smart farming, home automation, industrial control, security systems, wireless metering, and general IoT development.

Equipped with an ESP32-S3FN8 microprocessor, featuring a dual-core Xtensa® 32-bit LX7 CPU, five-stage pipeline, and clock speed up to 240 MHz. Integrated SX1262 LoRa chip for long-range wireless communication. USB Type-C interface with built-in voltage regulation, ESD protection, short-circuit protection, RF shielding, and other safety features. Includes an SH1.25-2 battery connector and a built-in lithium battery management system that supports charging, discharging, overcharge protection, battery level monitoring, and automatic power switching between USB and battery. Features a 0.96-inch OLED display (128×64 resolution) for showing debug info, battery status, and more. Supports Wi-Fi, LoRa, and Bluetooth connectivity. Comes with a built-in 2.4GHz metal spring antenna for Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, and a reserved IPEX (U.FL) port for LoRa. Uses the CP2102 USB-to-serial chip, making it easy to upload code and view debug output. Compatible with the Arduino development environment for quick and flexible programming. Designed with a high-quality RF circuit and low power consumption for efficient operation.

Parameters Description Master Chip ESP32-S3FN8 (Xtensa®32-bit lx7 dual core processor) LoRa Node Chip SX1262 USB to Serial Chip CP2102 Frequency 470-510MHz, 863-928MHz Max. TX Power 21±1dBm Max. Receiving sensitivity -134dBm@SF12 BW=125KHz Wi-Fi 802.11 b/g/n, up to 150Mbps Bluetooth Bluetooth 5 (LE) Hardware Resource 7 * ADC, 2 * ADC2, 7 * Touch,3 * UART, 2 * I2C, 2 * SPI, etc.. Memory 384KB ROM, 512KB SRAM, 16KB RTC SRAM, 8MB SiP Flash Interface Type-C USB, 2 * 1.25 battery interface, LoRa ANT(IPEX1.0), 2 * 18 * 2.54 Header Pin Battery 3.7V lithium battery power supply and charging Operating Temperature -20 ~ 70 ℃ Dimensions 50.2 * 25.5* 10.2 mm

LoRaWAN defines regional profiles such as EU868, US915, IN865, etc. Transmission power, channel bandwidth, and duty cycle regulations vary by country. Always ensure hardware certification (e.g., FCC, CE, MIC) and compliance with local laws.

India: Use 865–867 MHz band for license-free applications like smart metering, logistics, and agriculture. UK & EU: LoRa modules supporting 868 MHz can be deployed under ISM band rules with proper duty cycle compliance.

The N30 is the first maker-focused product developed by our Meshnology team, specifically designed for the Heltec LoRa V3 Node. It features a newly engineered, compact 3D-printed protective case along with a built-in 1100mAh battery. Despite its small footprint, the N30 seamlessly integrates both the Heltec LoRa V3 Node and the battery, achieving optimal balance between size and weight. It delivers a complete, ready-to-deploy solution for LoRa applications in outdoor environments.

documents.t: The Visual Line Tracking Demo implements the movement of the racing car within the track based on a purely visual method, with guiding lines in the middle of the track assisting the car to stay within the track.

To achieve the above function, three main modules are needed: Visual Input Environment Perception Motion Control These modules interact as follows: The Visual Input module obtains images of the real world (or simulated world) and passes them to the environment perception module. The Environment Perception module analyzes the position of the racing car on the track and sends relevant information to the motion control module. The Motion Control module calculates motion control commands based on the car’s position and sends them to the chassis for execution.

NodeHub is the Intelligent Robot Application Center provided by Horizon for robot developers. It contains open-source Nodes with various functions that can be quickly installed and used. By connecting different Nodes, the implementation of the above three modules can be completed.

In the Peripheral Adaptation section of NodeHub, various sensors and robot chassis adaptations are available to easily acquire image and point cloud data. Here, select MIPI Camera Driver to implement the visual input module.

Supports the GC4663 wide-angle camera, providing a larger field of view beneficial for line tracking. Supports multiple resolutions: 1920×1080, 640×480. Publishes topics: /hbmem_image /image_raw /camera_info
Use the following launch file for balanced performance: Publishes 640×480 NV12 images via shared memory.

sudo apt update sudo apt install -y tros-mipi-cam source /opt/tros/setup.bash ros2 launch mipi_cam mipi_cam_640x480_nv12_hbmem.launch.py sudo apt update sudo apt install -y tros-racing-track-detection-resnet source /opt/tros/setup.bash ros2 launch racing_track_detection_resnet racing_track_detection_resnet.launch.py sudo apt update sudo apt install -y tros-racing-control source /opt/tros/local_setup.bash ros2 launch racing_control racing_control.launch.py \ avoid_angular_ratio:=0.2 \ avoid_linear_speed:=0.1 \ follow_angular_ratio:=-1.0 \ follow_linear_speed:=0.1 sudo apt update sudo apt install -y tros-originbot-base tros-serial tros-originbot-msgs source /opt/tros/setup.bash ros2 launch originbot_base robot.launch.py MIPI Camera Driver → Track Detection → Car Line Following Control → Chassis Driver │ │ │ │ (Images) (Track Center) (Velocity Cmds) (Motor Control)

Visit Meshtastic Web Flasher. For L1, L1 Lite, and L1 Pro, select the target device as Seeed Wio Tracker L1 and choose the latest firmware, then click Flash. For L1 E-Ink, select the target device as Seeed Wio Tracker L1 E-Ink and choose the latest firmware, then click Flash. Open it, click Enter DFU Mode, and a device named Tracker L1 will appear. Click on it and connect to it. A drive named Tracker L1 should be displayed. Drag the UF2 file to the DFU drive. After the file download is complete, the firmware should be flashed, and the device will restart.

Start​ Connect the USB cable to activate the device. Flick the power switch upwards to turn it on. ❗Prompt If the device does not respond when you press the button, please charge it first. Do not use a fast-charging charger. Through application iOS application Select the target device on the Bluetooth panel. Input the code displayed on the screen, and then click OK to connect the device. Android app Click + and select the target device. Input the code (the default code is 123456), and then click OK to connect the device. Through the website​ If you wish to send text messages and communicate with other nodes on the website, you can now connect your device to the Meshtastic website. Step 1: Open the website clickGo to this website. Step 2: Add a new device Click "+ New Connection". There are two connection methods. You can choose the one you prefer. Method 1: Via Bluetooth Select the Bluetooth method. Choose the device ID in the pop-up window. Method 2: Through serial port Select the serial port mode. Open the Device Manager to check which port the device is connected to. Select that port in the pop-up window. Your device will be displayed in the list. Click to connect. If the connection is successful, you can directly view the device status on the website. Configuration​ In order to start communicating through the mesh, you must set the region. This setting controls the frequency range used by your device and should be set according to your fault. iOS application Android application Now that you have set up the LoRa region on your device, you can proceed to configure any LoRa settings to meet your specific needs. Configure GPS​ Please enable GPS. You can adjust the update interval and broadcast interval to obtain more timely location information. For iOS, please enable Accurate Location. Description​ After the device is turned on, it will automatically shut down or restart after a period of time. The serial port log stops after running for a period of time. This may be caused by manually forcing a restart or shutdown of the device when it is in the following states: unfinished message transmission process, or in the process of configuration ..... Troubleshooting​ Click here to watch the video. You need to perform a flash erase and then re-flash the latest firmware.

If you wish to revert to the default settings, you can perform a factory reset. There are two methods to perform a factory reset. Click here to watch the video. You need to perform a flash erase and then re-flash the latest firmware. Click the Factory Reset button in the app. The device will automatically restart using its factory settings.

SNR reflects the quality of the communication link. Normal devices usually operate above -7 dB. Devices with SNR below -10 dB indicate poor performance. RSSI is determined by both the device and its surrounding environment. Normal devices typically operate above -110 dBm. Devices with RSSI below -115 dBm are considered to have poor performance. To achieve the best signal effect, please use the device in an open, unobstructed area with minimal interference.

It all started in a small workshop cluttered with wires, circuit boards, and endless cups of coffee. A group of makers, tinkerers, and engineers sat around a table, not just discussing technology—but reimagining it. We weren’t satisfied with just using hardware; we wanted to create it, improve it, and most importantly, share it. That’s when we discovered RoLa open-source hardware—a system full of potential, waiting to be explored. But we didn’t stop at using it. We saw a new horizon, a chance to push the boundaries of open-source design and make something uniquely ours. And so, Meshnology was born.

Our journey wasn’t smooth. There were nights spent debugging circuits that refused to cooperate, days when prototypes failed spectacularly, and moments of doubt. But every failure was a lesson, every challenge an opportunity. We weren’t just building products—we were laying the foundation for a new era of open-source innovation. Today, Meshnology stands for more than just hardware. It represents a belief that technology should be accessible, adaptable, and limitless. Our products are not just tools; they are invitations—for makers, students, engineers, and dreamers—to take what we’ve built and make it even better.

We don’t create for the sake of selling. We create to inspire. To push the limits of what’s possible. To transform makers into innovators. Welcome to Meshnology. The future is open, and it’s yours to build.

At the Meshnology store, we offer LoRa protocol-based node products, including our flagship N30 series. This series provides a complete solution—enclosure, battery, and antenna—for nodes like the Heltec WiFi & LoRa V3, making it easier for makers to apply LoRa technology in Meshtatics and IoT applications. Of course, the enclosures and batteries in the N30 series are also available separately, giving makers greater flexibility for DIY projects. In addition, we sell products independently developed by the Meshnology team, such as load testers and keypad modules, to support a comprehensive product ecosystem for the maker community.
